note: _non consideres personam pauperis, nec honores vultum potentis_ – respect not the person of the poor, nor honour the countenance of the mighty. Both _persona_ and _facies_ translate Hebrew _pānîm_, “face.” As often, Jerome varies, as required by good Latin style. _Persona_ means here “the exterior of the human individual” (das Äußere des Menschen), see Hans Rheinfelder: _Das Wort “Persona.” Geschichte seiner Bedeutung._ Halle 1928 (xiii, 200 pp.), p. 81.
